title: Flower simulation client identity derived via node_id % 4 collided/misassigned partitions
summary: In 3/3 sampled Flower simulation guard runs before the fix, large/random simulation node IDs mapped via modulo-4 produced partition/client misassignments and duplicate client assignments, so at least one canonical client partition was never trained and another trained multiple times in every run. The old guard counted nodes/results, not partition identities, and could not detect this.

old_behavior_commit_range.notes: client_app.py and strategy.py derived identity via node_id % len(CLIENT_IDS) before fix commits 3ee2266/31deb5e/f5043a6/6299b71.

theoretical_risk: For 4 random nodes assigned to 4 modulo buckets, P(not a perfect identity assignment) = 1 - 4!/4^4 = 90.625%.

impact.invalid: Any result produced through the Flower simulation app path (flwr run/guard/Flower ClientApp/ServerApp) before the fix is invalid for 4-partition identity/per-client attribution claims; '4 results received' counted nodes, not distinct partitions.
impact.unaffected: In-process FedAvg+FedBN shipped-model reference and artifacts computed in-process (not via Flower flwr run simulation app path), including reports/is_high_risk_auc.json and artifacts/fairness_disparity.json as currently reported, are not affected by Flower simulation node_id mapping.

remediation.client: Resolve identity from Flower node_config partition-id/num-partitions with assertions/logging; report canonical client_id in fit/eval metrics.
remediation.server: Learn node_id->client_id from reported replies (bootstrap all when unknown), reject unknown/conflicting/duplicate identities with audit events, support dropout by default and require_all_clients only for guard/proof.
remediation.guard: Run with require-all-clients and parse CLIENT_MAPPING/CLIENT_PHASE_FIT/CLIENT_PHASE_EVALUATE to fail unless exactly the 4 canonical clients participate once each in fit and evaluate.
remediation.tests: Revert-fail unit tests for resolver/strategy invariants and secagg identity-inactive behavior added.
